newsitem.title: USA: AT&T Business Network shutting down.
newsitem.headline: AT&T Business Network shutting down.

text.p: The AT&T Business Network Web site that offers a wealth of business information is closing down, the Internet company that ran it under license from AT&T Corp. said Monday.

Nets Inc. spokeswoman Jennifer Christensen said the Web site (http://www.bnet.att.com), which remained active Monday, was no longer being updated on a daily basis. The site is slated to close its doors by the beginning of April, she said.
Nets on Thursday told employees it was closing down the Web site and that it would cut 54 of the company's 304 jobs.
The company said Monday it was seeking additional investors but was not ready to make an initial public offering.

"I don't think it's a secret that we're seeking additional investors, but there is not going to be an IPO anytime soon," Christensen said, adding more work was needed to prepare the company for a public offering.

Nets, whose biggest shareholders include former Lotus Develepment Corp. Chief Executive Jim Manzi, is planning to build a business-to-business electronic commerce operation to help maintenance and repair organisations buy parts.

In an e-mail memo to staff members made available to Reuters, Manzi said the company expects to at least double revenue in 1997 and gain 200,000 new customers. The memo did not give figures for 1996 revenue or customers.
He also said the company would get out of its target marketing business.
If it is successful serving the market for industrial components in areas like air conditioning and heating, it will replicate its approach in new markets, Manzi's memo said.
